summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple sclerosis and a chronic indwelling Foley catheter, was admitted with fever and fatigue due to sepsis. The infection source was determined to be a combination of a severely infected stage IV sacral pressure ulcer with underlying osteomyelitis and a urinary tract infection. He underwent surgical debridement of the ulcer and was started on intravenous vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam. Blood cultures revealed skin flora, supporting a wound origin, and he improved clinically with normalization of inflammatory markers. A PICC line was placed for six weeks of outpatient antibiotic therapy. He was discharged to an extended care facility for wound care and rehabilitation, with plans to follow up with infectious disease and urology, the latter to discuss suprapubic catheter placement given recurrent urosepsis. Nutritional support and mental health resources were also arranged.
